messages:
hana: quick lint fail on staging: /v1/generate examples use `stop` as string in JSON but the schema expects `stop` to be an array of strings. failing example at line ~88.

ben: can you paste the example? i'll fix.

hana: failing snippet:

```json
{
  "input": "Summarize this",
  "stop": "\n\n",
  "max_new_tokens": 64
}
```

oli: that's the issue. OpenAPI is `stop: string[]`. the runtime historically accepted either, but docs should show the canonical array form and mention the legacy single-string compatibility. suggested fix:

```json
{
  "input": "Summarize this",
  "stop": ["\n\n"],
  "max_new_tokens": 64
}
```

ci-bot: docs linter error: docs/generate.md: example-schema-mismatch (line 88).

ben: opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/900 - updates examples to use array form, adds a one-line migration note: "If you have a single stop string, wrap it in an array (e.g. ['\\n\\n'])." also adds a fixture test.

hana: please also update the JS + Python snippets that showed `stop: ""` inline. small doc tweak: explain why arrays are preferred (multiple stop tokens).

oli: updated both snippets and added a short sentence in the API note. CI checks passed.

ci-bot: PR checks: lint ✅, examples test ✅, staging build ✅.

ben: merged. thanks folks. saved a confusing example.
